title: 319. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Identifying Points Lines Rays and Segments
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the geometric object that has no size and is represented by a dot.
questions.question: Which of the following best describes a point in geometry?

options.label: A
options.text: A location that has no size and is usually represented by a dot.

options.label: B
options.text: A straight path that extends infinitely in both directions.

questions.explanation: In geometry, a point indicates a location. It has no length, width, or thickness and is usually drawn as a dot. A straight path extending infinitely in both directions is a line, not a point.
questions.hint: Think about the most basic geometric object that only marks a position.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the geometric figure that has one endpoint and extends infinitely in one direction.
questions.question: Which figure is a ray?

options.label: B
options.text: A figure with one endpoint that extends infinitely in one direction.

questions.explanation: A ray has exactly one endpoint and extends without end in one direction. A figure with two endpoints is a line segment, not a ray.
questions.hint: A ray starts at one point and goes on forever in only one direction.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize a line segment as part of a line with two endpoints.
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a line segment?

options.label: A
options.text: It extends infinitely in both directions.

options.label: B
options.text: It is part of a line with two endpoints.

questions.explanation: A line segment is a portion of a line bounded by two distinct endpoints. A figure extending infinitely in both directions is a line, not a segment.
questions.hint: A segment has a definite beginning and end.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize a line as a straight path extending infinitely in both directions.
questions.question: Which figure represents a line?

options.label: A
options.text: A straight path with two endpoints.

options.label: B
options.text: A straight path that extends infinitely in both directions.

questions.explanation: A line is a straight path that has no endpoints and extends infinitely in both directions. A path with two endpoints is a segment.
questions.hint: A line continues without stopping in both directions.

questions.concept: Naming a Ray from Its Endpoint and Direction
questions.learningObjective: Identify the correct notation for a ray starting at point A and passing through point B.
questions.question: A ray starts at point \(A\) and passes through point \(B\). Which notation represents this ray?
questions.explanation: The notation \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) denotes the ray that starts at \(A\) and passes through \(B\). The endpoint is written first. \(\overrightarrow{BA}\) would start at \(B\), which is incorrect for the described ray.
questions.hint: The first letter in ray notation is the endpoint.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a set of collinear points.
questions.question: Which set of points is collinear?

options.label: A
options.text: Points that do not all lie on one straight line.

options.label: B
options.text: Points that lie on the same line.

questions.explanation: Collinear points all belong to one straight line. Option B states this defining property; option A explicitly denies it.
questions.hint: Break the term into its reference to a shared straight geometric object.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the intersection of two distinct lines.
questions.question: Two distinct lines intersect at exactly one point. What is this intersection?
questions.explanation: Two distinct non-parallel lines meet at exactly one location. That location is a single point. A line segment would require two endpoints, which is not the case for the intersection of two lines.
questions.hint: Think about where two straight lines cross.

questions.learningObjective: Identify opposite rays from a given point.
questions.question: Point \(O\) lies strictly between the distinct points \(A\) and \(B\) on line \(AB\). Which rays are opposite rays?
questions.explanation: Opposite rays share the same endpoint and extend in exactly opposite directions, forming a straight line. \(\overrightarrow{OA}\) and \(\overrightarrow{OB}\) share endpoint \(O\) and point in opposite directions. \(\overrightarrow{OA}\) and \(\overrightarrow{AO}\) do not share the same endpoint.
questions.hint: Opposite rays start at the same point and point in opposite directions.

questions.concept: Length of a Segment with a Point Between
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the length of a segment using the segment addition postulate.
questions.question: Point \(B\) lies between points \(A\) and \(C\) on segment \(AC\). If \(AB = 5\) and \(BC = 3\), what is \(AC\)?
questions.explanation:
By the segment addition postulate, if \(B\) is between \(A\) and \(C\), then
\[
AC = AB + BC = 5 + 3 = 8.
\]
Therefore, \(AC = 8\).
questions.hint: Add the lengths of the two smaller segments.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the total length of a segment given its midpoint and half-length.
questions.question: \(M\) is the midpoint of segment \(AB\). If \(AM = 4\), what is \(AB\)?
questions.explanation:
A midpoint divides a segment into two equal parts, so
\[
AM = MB = 4.
\]
Thus
\[
AB = AM + MB = 4 + 4 = 8.
\]
Therefore, \(AB = 8\).
questions.hint: The midpoint splits the segment into two equal parts.
